assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear, original discovery with a sharp theoretical prediction: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at a magic twist angle, and the correlated-insulator and superconducting states observed in twisted bilayer graphene opened a whole field of moire quantum matter. Impact on condensed-matter physics is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: The theory credit to MacDonald and Bistritzer and the experimental credit to Jarillo-Herrero form a natural theory-plus-experiment prize. Other contributors (for example Cory Dean's group, Kim, Young, Yazdani) are not in the credited names and some may argue for them; I rely on my own recollection of this history rather than independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Experiment reproduced by many groups since 2018 and the framework is stable. The field is still moving fast, but the core discovery is mature and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the credit should extend to the experimental groups that first established the correlated and superconducting states at scale.
Which of the many follow-on phases (fractional Chern insulators, etc.) belong to the same prize remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of the Higgs boson was the central experimental discovery of modern particle physics, completing the Standard Model. The discovery rested on the conception and construction of ATLAS and CMS, which is an invention-and-discovery story in its own right.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize recognised the theoretical prediction. For the experiment, the credited names are founding figures of ATLAS and CMS; this is a defensible but imperfect configuration given the thousands of collaborators and the key roles of the spokespersons during the 2012 discovery, who are not credited here. The collaboration-attribution problem is real and I do not consider it resolved.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and independently reproduced by two experiments, with couplings measured at the percent to ten-percent level since 2012. Recognition of the experiment is long established as a topic and certainly not premature.
uncertainties: Whether a prize to founders rather than to discovery-period leaders fairly reflects the decisive contributions.
Statute limits on three laureates and the exclusion of the collaborations as such.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators are a foundational concept in modern condensed matter: a new topological classification of band insulators with protected edge and surface states, predicted theoretically and then observed in HgTe quantum wells and in bismuth-based three-dimensional materials. Originality and lasting influence are high.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theory, Molenkamp's group the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect, Hasan's group the first 3D topological insulators. Eugene J. Mele, and outside the credited names Bernevig, Zhang and others, make the allocation contested; the three-laureate cap forces a choice among strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed many times across materials and techniques over nearly two decades. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority questions between the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang predictions, partly beyond the supplied credit list.
Whether the 3D and 2D discoveries should be treated as one compound prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered precision measurements of the CMB anisotropies that established the Lambda-CDM standard model of cosmology, fixing the age, geometry and composition of the universe. This is a discovery-driven result of the type the committee values, with a very large and lasting impact on cosmology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett as principal investigator, Spergel as lead on the cosmological interpretation and Page as instrument scientist is a coherent trio. Other WMAP team members (for example Wilkinson, deceased) and the roles of Planck and COBE-era results complicate matters. The 2006 and 2019 prizes already recognised cosmology and CMB work, which may reduce the appetite.
assessment.maturity: Results were confirmed and improved by Planck and ground-based experiments; the interpretation is stable. Mature, with the timing question being competition from earlier cosmology prizes rather than premature recognition.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the cosmology area as already recently recognised.
Relative weight of the experiment-versus-analysis contributions inside a large collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model and the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition, creating quantum simulators for strongly correlated matter. The idea (Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators) and its experimental realisation are both of high originality, and the impact on many-body physics and quantum technologies is large.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Cirac and Jaksch) for the theoretical proposals, Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger for the experiments. Five credited names exceed the cap, so I choose Bloch, Esslinger and Zoller while acknowledging that Greiner and Cirac have strong claims. I have not independently verified who was first on each experiment.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many laboratories for over twenty years, with continued progress in quantum-gas microscopes. Mature and not premature, although the 2001 and 2012 prizes touched the neighbouring areas.
uncertainties: Allocation among five strong candidates; Cirac is also credited under trapped ions in another candidate.
Overlap with earlier BEC and quantum optics prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube, followed by evidence for a blazar source and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as a real observational window. It is a clear discovery with lasting impact for astrophysics and particle physics.
assessment.attribution: Only one name is supplied. Halzen was the main driving force of IceCube, but a discovery of this scale was enabled by a large collaboration and by earlier work (AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND) and by other leaders; a one-person prize would be a narrow reading. I cannot verify the finer allocation of credit.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux was seen at high significance in 2013 and confirmed by independent analyses; source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) is more recent but strengthening. Recognition is plausible now.
uncertainties: Fair attribution when only one credited name is available, and the role of collaboration leaders such as the spokespersons.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional precision, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, give a new level of precision for tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a future redefinition of the second. The result is original and clearly measurable.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the lattice-clock concept and Ye achieved the leading precision with strontium; the two-person configuration is clean. Contributions from other groups (NIST, PTB, SYRTE) and the 2005 and 2012 prizes in related areas may be mentioned.
assessment.maturity: Demonstrated independently in several laboratories, with the second redefinition process in progress; maturity is high and timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees the field as already recognised through the frequency comb and ion-clock prizes.
Relative claims of other lattice-clock groups not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance underpin the possibility of scalable quantum computing, and the topological codes added deep connections to many-body physics. The conceptual originality is high.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane introduced the first codes, Kitaev the topological codes and anyonic ideas; others (Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Aharonov and Ben-Or, Preskill) have strong claims and the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are now appearing, including recent below-threshold surface-code results, but large-scale fault tolerance remains to be shown, so recognition could be seen as somewhat early for physics.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over many contributors beyond the three-name cap.
Whether the committee wants experimental maturity before honouring the theory.
